_note: filename -> CSS object-position, read by scripts/build_banners.py and
published into docs/data/church/banners.json as 'focal'. It is where the
page crops THIS image when the masthead's height cap bites.
Measured, not guessed, by the method panel's focal.json documents: the
art was overlaid with a 5% horizontal grid and the face band read off
it, then y set to the smallest object-position that puts the window's
top edge at or above that band at the widest desktop band (1360px,
where the crop is deepest). Narrower viewports crop less, so a value
that clears the faces at 1360 clears them everywhere.
0% here is CHOSEN, not forced -- unlike browns_trophychase_01, whose
back row is cut by the source frame. At 1360 this 3:1 frame renders
453px tall and the 280px cap shows 61.8% of it, so the window is
0-61.8% and the faces at 15-46% sit inside it with 15% of frame clear
above and 16% clear below: as close to centred as the value can get.
Anything up to 39% still clears the band, but every step down trades
the trophy's crown -- which starts at ~3% -- for floor and dust.
The five reaching hands, at 48-62%, stay in frame either way.
